key_insight: By concatenating GKP and Steane error-correcting codes, the paper shows that an all-photonic repeater can reach 1,000 km communication with 9 km spacing while staying more resilient to photon loss.
engineering_relevance: The design lowers repeater-node resource demands to only a few thousand GKP qubits per station per run, making large-scale quantum network deployment more practical.
method: All-photonic repeater architecture with equidistant 9 km spacing
Concatenated bosonic GKP + [[7,1,3]] Steane codes for improved loss tolerance
Heuristic Bell-pair construction plus optical-cavity memory and switching-imperfection modeling
evidence_signal: Simulations incorporating standard optical imperfections and switching-induced errors indicate the proposed scheme can meet the target with substantially fewer GKP qubits than prior third-generation all-photonic repeater designs.
watch_item: Performance depends on realistic control of optical imperfections, cavity mirror efficiency, and switching-induced errors, which may be challenging to achieve experimentally.
paper_title: High-Rate and Resource-Efficient All-Photonic Quantum Repeater Architectures with 9 km Repeater Spacing
